subject: AI & Agents
title: What Makes a Language Model 'Large'
description: A fast breakdown of What Makes a Language Model 'Large' for builders.

hook.text: GPT-3 has 175 billion parameters. GPT-4 reportedly has over a trillion. What are all those numbers?

buildup.text: Parameters are adjustable weights inside the neural network — the knobs the model learns to tune.

discovery.text: More parameters let the model capture more nuanced patterns in language.

twist.text: Bigger isn't always better. A poorly trained large model can perform worse than a small one.

climax.text: The magic isn't just size — it's the combination of scale, data quality, and training technique.

punchline.text: Size matters, but only with the right recipe.

quiz.question: What are parameters in a language model?
options: Adjustable weights the model learns during training
The number of languages it supports

details.summary: A language model becomes 'large' when it has billions of parameters — the numerical weights learned during training. More parameters allow the model to store more knowledge and handle more complex tasks.
details.whyItMatters: Model size drives capability. Understanding what makes a model large explains the arms race in AI, the costs of development, and the tradeoff between bigger models and practical deployment.
takeaways: Parameters are the learned numerical weights inside the model
Large language models have billions to trillions of parameters
More parameters generally mean more capability but higher costs

faq.question: How many parameters do major LLMs have?
faq.answer: GPT-3 has 175 billion parameters. GPT-4 is estimated at over a trillion. Llama 3 comes in 8B, 70B, and 405B variants. The trend has been toward larger models, though smaller efficient models are now also advancing.

faq.question: Do more parameters always mean better performance?
faq.answer: Generally yes, up to a point. But training data quality, training techniques, and architecture also matter enormously. A well-trained smaller model can outperform a poorly trained larger one.
